**Observation Log:**

- [FACT] The user is designing a circuit board that houses a differential pressure transducer.
- [FACT] The user is using the differential pressure transducer to make pitot tube air speed velocity measurements.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant is happy to help the user create a schematic for the circuit board with a differential pressure transducer.
- [ASSISTANT_CREATED] The assistant provided a basic schematic for the circuit board, including components such as Vcc, R1, R2, R3, R4, C1, C2, and OUT.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant explained that the circuit uses an instrumentation amplifier to amplify the differential pressure signal from the transducer.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant mentioned that resistors R3 and R4 form a voltage divider to set the gain of the amplifier, with the gain formula G = 1 + 2R4/R3.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant noted that capacitors C1 and C2 filter out high-frequency noise, and resistors R1 and R2 provide a stable reference voltage (Vref) to the amplifier.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant advised consulting the datasheet for the transducer and amplifier to choose appropriate component values.
- [FACT] The user is designing a set of steering column stalks.
- [FACT] There isn't enough space inside the column to package the mechanical switches needed to take input from the stalk and convey it to the body controller.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant suggested using touch-sensitive capacitive sensors to make the stalks functional without mechanical switches.
- [ASSISTANT_CREATED] The assistant provided a basic schematic for a touch-sensitive capacitive sensor, including components such as C1, C2, and pins.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant explained that when a user touches a pin, their body forms a capacitor, changing the capacitance of the sensing circuit.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant mentioned using an operational amplifier (op-amp) configured as a capacitance-to-voltage converter to detect changes in capacitance.
- [ASSISTANT_CREATED] The assistant provided a schematic for an op-amp-based capacitance-to-voltage converter, including components such as C1, R1, R2, and OUT.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant explained that the output voltage of the op-amp is proportional to the change in capacitance and can be used as an input to a microcontroller.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant noted that the specific values of capacitors and resistors depend on the application requirements and the op-amp used.
- [USER] The user asked how to incorporate haptic feedback into the capacitive touch-sensitive stalks.
